questions.question: A ministry receives money to meet urgent financial expenses provided for in the recurrent budget, but the vouchers cannot immediately be presented to Treasury. The arrangement is—
questions.explanation: This is the source's definition of Imprest: money advanced to a government office for urgent recurrent-budget expenses where vouchers cannot immediately be presented to Treasury.

questions.question: How many kinds of Imprest are identified in the material?
questions.explanation: The material identifies two kinds: Standing Imprest and Special Imprest.

questions.question: An Imprest Warrant covers recurrent expenses for the whole financial year. Which type of Imprest does this describe?
questions.explanation: A Standing Imprest has a warrant covering the whole financial year for recurrent expenses.

questions.question: A Standing Imprest is issued at the beginning of the financial year. When, according to the material, is it normally retired?
options: At the end of the financial year, 31 December
At the beginning of the following financial year
questions.explanation: The source states that a Standing Imprest need not be retired until the end of the financial year, specifically 31 December.

questions.question: A Standing Imprest is replenished during the financial year. How is reimbursement described in the material?
options: The Treasury reimburses the same amount from time to time, usually monthly.
The officer receives reimbursement only after five years.
The reimbursement is made only when the project is completed.
No reimbursement occurs until the Standing Imprest is retired.
questions.explanation: The material states that as Standing Imprest is replenished, reimbursement of the same amount is made by Treasury from time to time, usually monthly, during the financial year.

questions.question: Which expenditure is given as an example of the ordinary use of Standing Imprest?
questions.explanation: The material specifically lists petrol for official vehicles, office stationery and other day-to-day office needs as uses of Standing Imprest.

questions.question: A ministry receives ₦500,000 under an Imprest Warrant that expressly states the money is to be used only for a particular project. Which classification applies?
questions.explanation: Special Imprest covers a specific purpose or project and nothing else; its warrant specifies what the money is to be used for.

questions.question: A Special Imprest is issued for a particular project. The project is completed in September. When should the Imprest be retired according to the material?
options: As soon as the purpose is completed, since this occurs before the end of the financial year
Automatically on 31 December regardless of completion
At the beginning of the next financial year
questions.explanation: Special Imprest should be retired when the purpose is completed or at the end of the financial year, whichever is sooner.

questions.question: Two Imprest arrangements are being compared: Arrangement X covers ordinary recurrent expenses for the whole financial year. Arrangement Y has a separate warrant for a specific project. Which classification is correct?
options: X — Standing Imprest; Y — Special Imprest
X — Special Imprest; Y — Standing Imprest
X — Personal Advance; Y — Non-personal Advance
X — Non-personal Advance; Y — Personal Advance
questions.explanation: Standing Imprest covers recurrent expenses throughout the financial year, whereas Special Imprest is tied to a specific purpose or project under a separate warrant.

questions.question: A ministry has four financial arrangements: A. An officer collects a particular form of government revenue using an official receipt book and keeps a Revenue Cash Book. B. An officer receives delegated control of a sub-head through an AIE. C. An officer other than a Sub-Accounting Officer disburses public money where vouchers cannot immediately be presented and keeps a Cash Book. D. An office receives a warrant covering recurrent expenses for the entire financial year. Which option correctly identifies A, B, C and D, respectively?
options: Revenue Officer; Officer Controlling Expenditure; Imprest Holder; Standing Imprest
Sub-Accounting Officer; Revenue Officer; Standing Imprest; Special Imprest
Revenue Officer; Imprest Holder; Officer Controlling Expenditure; Special Imprest
Imprest Holder; Officer Controlling Expenditure; Revenue Officer; Standing Imprest
questions.explanation: A → Revenue Officer: regular collection of a particular revenue using an official receipt/licence book and Revenue Cash Book. B → Officer Controlling Expenditure: delegated control of a sub-head through an AIE. C → Imprest Holder: an officer other than a Sub-Accounting Officer entrusted with the specified public-money disbursement and required to keep a Cash Book. D → Standing Imprest: warrant covering recurrent expenses for the whole financial year.

questions.question: According to the material, the MTEF takes into consideration the requirement that government spending should not exceed revenue by more than—
questions.explanation: The material states that the MTEF takes into consideration the legal requirement that spending should not exceed revenue by more than 3% of GDP.

questions.question: A State financial planner proposes an expenditure framework that would cause government spending to exceed revenue by 6% of GDP. Based strictly on the MTEF requirement stated in the material, the proposal—
options: is automatically acceptable because it is within 10%
is acceptable provided the House of Assembly agrees
questions.explanation: The material specifically states that spending should not exceed revenue by more than 3% of GDP within the MTEF framework.

questions.question: The MTEF shifts the psychology of budgeting from "needs" to—
questions.explanation: The material expressly describes this as a key effect of the MTEF: moving budgeting thinking from "needs" to the "availability of resources."

questions.question: A government department submits a long list of desired projects without considering the resources available to fund them. Which MTEF principle would require the department to reconsider its approach?
options: Budgeting should take account of the availability of resources.
Every identified need must automatically be funded.
Capital expenditure must always exceed recurrent expenditure.
questions.explanation: The material says the MTEF shifts the psychology of budgeting from identifying "needs" to considering the availability of resources.

questions.question: Under the Fiscal Responsibility Law provisions cited in the material, the State and Local Governments are required to develop a—
options: Fiscal Strategic Paper within an MTEF for the next three years
Payment Voucher for the next three years
Public Accounts Committee report every three years
Revenue Cash Book for the next three years
questions.explanation: The material states that Part V, Sections 15–21 of the Fiscal Responsibility Law mandate the State and Local Government to develop a Fiscal Strategic Paper (FSP) within an MTEF for the next three years.

questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the matters specifically listed for possible public consultation during preparation of the MTEF?
options: Strategic, economic, social and developmental priorities of government
The personal financial affairs of individual public officers
questions.explanation: The material lists the macro-economic framework, fiscal strategy document, government priorities and other matters the Commissioner may deem necessary. Personal financial affairs of officers are not listed.

questions.question: The Commissioner for Economic Development decides to consult the public while preparing the MTEF. Which group is expressly included in the consultation audience?
options: Only members of the House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The material states that consultation should be open to the public, press, citizens, organizations/groups of citizens, professional bodies, unions and others.

questions.question: A professional body requests to participate in consultation on the MTEF. Based on the material, the request—
options: falls within the categories expressly contemplated for consultation
is limited to procurement matters only
can only be accepted after an audit
questions.explanation: Professional bodies are expressly listed among those to whom MTEF consultations should be open.

questions.question: The Honourable Commissioner for Economic Development is preparing the MTEF. By what point in the financial year must he present it?
options: Before the end of the second quarter
After the House passes the Appropriation Law
After the annual accounts are audited
questions.explanation: The material requires the Commissioner for Economic Development to present the MTEF before the end of the second quarter of each financial year.

questions.question: The State Executive Council has endorsed the MTEF. What additional event is required before it takes effect?
options: Approval by the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly
Approval by the Public Accounts Committee
questions.explanation: The MTEF, as endorsed by the State Executive Council, takes effect upon approval by the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between the MTEF and the annual budget?
options: The MTEF provides the basis for preparing the revenue and expenditure estimates presented to the State House of Assembly.
The annual budget provides the basis for preparing the MTEF after it has been approved.
The MTEF replaces the annual budget completely.
questions.explanation: The material expressly states that the MTEF shall be the basis for preparing estimates of revenue and expenditure to be presented to the State House of Assembly.

questions.question: A ministry prepares its annual revenue and expenditure estimates without considering the approved MTEF. Which principle in the material has the ministry failed to observe?
options: The MTEF should form the basis for preparation of the annual revenue and expenditure estimates.
The annual budget must always precede the MTEF.
The MTEF applies only to capital expenditure.
The MTEF is relevant only to auditing.
questions.explanation: The source explicitly establishes the MTEF as the basis for preparation of the annual revenue and expenditure estimates.

questions.question: A public entity is funded partly from the State Treasury and partly from internally generated revenue. It argues that the Public Procurement Law does not apply because its funding is mixed. Which conclusion is supported by the material?
options: The funding arrangement does not remove it from the stated procurement scope.
Mixed funding automatically exempts an entity.
Only entities funded exclusively from the State Treasury are covered.
Only entities funded exclusively from IGR are covered.
questions.explanation: The procurement scope expressly includes entities funded by the State Treasury, internally generated revenue, the Consolidated Revenue Fund or special allocations from Federal or State Treasury.

questions.question: A government-owned corporation is procuring services, while a State University is procuring works. Which statement is consistent with the source?
options: Both procurement activities fall within the categories covered by the Public Procurement Law.
Only the corporation's procurement is covered.
Only procurement of goods is covered.
Neither is covered because both are corporate entities.
questions.explanation: The material states that the Procurement Law provides guidelines for procurement of goods, works and services and expressly includes Government-owned Corporations and State Universities and Colleges among covered entities.

questions.question: An auditor is examining whether a government entity has properly maintained its financial records. Which broader audit objective from the material is being addressed?
options: Ascertaining that proper accounts have been kept
Determining whether all officers received their allowances
Determining whether every project generated profit
questions.explanation: The State Auditor-General's responsibilities include ascertaining that proper accounts have been kept.

questions.question: During an audit, an officer cannot account for a portion of government money received. Which audit concern does this directly trigger?
options: Whether all monies have been fully accounted for
Whether the MTEF contains a macro-economic framework
Whether the procurement law covers services
Whether the budget call circular was issued
questions.explanation: The material states that the State Auditor-General audits public accounts to ascertain that all monies have been fully accounted for.

questions.question: An audit discovers that an MDA's financial transactions were properly recorded, but several applicable financial rules were not followed. Which audit criterion has not been satisfied?
questions.explanation: The Auditor-General's audit includes ascertaining that rules and regulations have been complied with.

questions.question: The Auditor-General has completed an audit and prepared a report expressing his opinion. Which body receives the report according to the material?
options: Public Accounts Committee of the State House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The material states that the Auditor-General's report, which expresses his opinion, is submitted to the Public Accounts Committee of the State House of Assembly.

questions.question: The PAC receives an Auditor-General's report containing a financial discrepancy. Which action is expressly within the PAC's stated role?
options: Investigating the financial matter and summoning public officials to explain discrepancies
Issuing an AIE to the affected officer
questions.explanation: The material states that the PAC can summon public officials to explain discrepancies and conduct investigations into financial matters.

questions.question: A State financial-management scenario unfolds as follows: The Commissioner for Economic Development prepares a three-year MTEF. The framework considers the resource-availability principle and the stated 3%-of-GDP spending constraint. Public consultation is opened to citizens, professional bodies and unions. The State Executive Council endorses the MTEF. The House of Assembly approves it. Annual revenue and expenditure estimates are subsequently prepared on its basis. At year-end, the Accountant-General prepares the Final Accounts. The State Auditor-General audits them and submits his report to the PAC. The PAC investigates a discrepancy and summons the responsible officials. Which statement best describes the entire sequence?
options: It connects medium-term fiscal planning, annual budgeting, accounting, audit and legislative financial oversight.
It represents only the public procurement process.
It represents only the imprest retirement process.
It represents only the collection of recurrent revenue.
questions.explanation: Each stage corresponds to a distinct part of the financial-management framework in the material: MTEF preparation and approval, annual budgeting based on the MTEF, preparation of Final Accounts by the Accountant-General, audit by the State Auditor-General and PAC oversight/investigation.

questions.question: Government revenue is generated primarily to enable government to—
options: run administration and execute development projects across sectors
questions.explanation: The material states that government generates revenue to run the administration of Federal, State and Local Governments and to execute development projects across sectors of the economy.

questions.question: According to the material, government revenue is ultimately allocated to spending organizations through the—
questions.explanation: Government revenue is generated through efficient and effective machinery and allocated through the budgetary system to spending organizations for their operations.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) in the material?
questions.explanation: IGR includes taxes, fines and fees, licences, earnings and sales, rents of government property, dividends and interest on investments.

questions.question: A State Government earns money from rents on government property. How is this revenue classified under the source?
questions.explanation: Rents of Government property are specifically listed under Internally Generated Revenue, which the material places under recurrent revenue.

questions.question: Which of the following is specifically identified as a source of revenue from the Federation Account?
questions.explanation: Revenue from the Federation Account includes Statutory Allocation, Value Added Tax, Excess Crude Oil Revenue and electronic money transfer (EMT), among others listed.

questions.question: A government financial officer is classifying an external loan received by government. Based on the material, the appropriate classification is—
questions.explanation: Internal and external loans are listed under Capital Receipts.

questions.question: Which combination contains only capital receipts identified in the material?
options: Internal loans, external loans, grants and ecological funds
questions.explanation: Capital receipts include transfers from Consolidated Revenue Funds, internal and external loans, ecological funds, grants and miscellaneous receipts.

questions.question: A government department receives a general grant. According to the source, this should be classified under—
questions.explanation: Specific and general grants are expressly listed among capital receipts.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes recurrent revenue from capital receipts as presented in the material?
options: Recurrent revenue includes IGR and Federation Account revenue, while capital receipts include items such as loans, grants and ecological funds.
Recurrent revenue consists only of loans.
Capital receipts consist only of taxes and fees.
There is no distinction between the two.
questions.explanation: The material places IGR and Federation Account revenue under recurrent revenue, while transfers, loans, ecological funds and grants are listed under capital receipts.

questions.question: A State Government receives the following: Tax revenue Rent from government property External loan General grant Which classification is correct?
options: 1 and 2 — Recurrent Revenue; 3 and 4 — Capital Receipts
1 and 3 — Recurrent Revenue; 2 and 4 — Capital Receipts
1 and 4 — Capital Receipts; 2 and 3 — Recurrent Revenue
questions.explanation: Taxes and rents of government property are included in IGR/recurrent revenue, while external loans and grants are listed under capital receipts.

questions.question: Government expenditure is divided in the material into—
questions.explanation: The source expressly states that government expenditures are of two types: Recurrent and Capital.

questions.question: Which description best fits recurrent expenditure?
options: Ongoing costs required for the daily functioning of government and maintenance of public service
Expenditure exclusively on assets providing benefits for more than one year
Government loans received from external sources
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure is described as ongoing costs necessary for daily government functioning and maintenance of public service.

questions.question: A ministry spends money regularly on salaries, office supplies, utilities and maintenance. These expenditures are most appropriately classified as—
questions.explanation: The material identifies salaries and wages, office supplies and utilities, maintenance and repairs and similar ongoing costs as recurrent expenditure.

questions.question: Which characteristic is associated with recurrent expenditure in the material?
options: It is regular, predictable and necessary for continuous government operations.
It always creates a physical asset.
It is received as a government loan.
It is necessarily funded from external grants.
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure is described as regular, predictable and necessary for continuous operation of government departments and agencies.

questions.question: A government expenditure involves constructing infrastructure expected to provide benefits over a long period. Which classification applies?
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure relates to assets that provide benefits over a long period, typically more than one year, including infrastructure projects.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of capital expenditure identified in the material?
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure includes infrastructure projects, equipment and machinery, land and buildings and development projects.

questions.question: A government investment creates an asset expected to provide benefits for more than one year. The classification is based primarily on the fact that the expenditure—
options: creates or enhances a long-term asset
is paid through a Revenue Cash Book
questions.explanation: The material defines capital expenditure in terms of spending on assets that provide benefits over a long period, typically more than one year, including acquisition, construction or enhancement of physical assets and infrastructure.

questions.question: The State Budget Office and Ministry of Economic Development issue budget call circulars to MDAs primarily to—
options: invite them to submit proposals for the coming year
questions.explanation: The budget process begins with recurrent and capital budget call circulars inviting Ministries and Departments to submit proposals for the coming year.

questions.question: A Permanent Secretary/Head of an Extra-Ministerial Department establishes a budget committee. What is the committee expected to provide?
questions.explanation: Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Departments constitute budget committees for MDAs to provide their quantitative forecasts.

questions.question: An MDA receives its budget call circular and establishes its budget committee. The committee prepares estimates covering: recurrent expenditure; capital expenditure; recurrent receipts; and capital receipts. The estimates are submitted to the Budget Office, which vets them and invites the MDA to defend its submission. What stage of the budget process does this scenario represent?
options: MDA preparation, submission and Budget Office vetting/defence of estimates
questions.explanation: The source states that after budget call circulars are issued, MDA budget committees provide quantitative forecasts and prepare estimates of recurrent/capital expenditure and receipts. The Budget Office then vets the estimates and invites each MDA to justify or defend its submission.

questions.question: A government financial officer needs an official authorization permitting the release or expenditure of public funds in accordance with the budgetary and legal framework. What instrument is required?
questions.explanation: A warrant is an official authorization issued by the Honourable Commissioner for Finance on behalf of the Governor to the Accountant-General permitting the release or expenditure of public funds.

questions.question: The principal control purpose of a warrant is to ensure that public funds are—
options: disbursed in accordance with the budgetary and legal framework
questions.explanation: The source states that warrants ensure funds are disbursed in accordance with the government's budgetary and legal framework and serve as a control mechanism.

questions.question: Which official issues the warrant described in the material?
options: The Honourable Commissioner for Finance, on behalf of the Governor
The State Auditor-General, on behalf of the PAC
The Head of Budget Office, on behalf of the House of Assembly
The Permanent Secretary, on behalf of the Accountant-General
questions.explanation: The material specifically states that the warrant is issued by the Honourable Commissioner for Finance on behalf of the Governor to the Accountant-General.

questions.question: A ministry wants to make a payment but has no evidence that funds are available under the approved budget. Which payment requirement has not been satisfied?
options: Evidence of availability of funds through a duly issued warrant or AIE
Attachment of the payee's official receipt
questions.explanation: The payment procedure requires evidence of availability of funds as provided in the budget through a warrant or AIE duly issued by the State Budget Office.

questions.question: Before a payment voucher proceeds through the payment process, it must be entered in the—
questions.explanation: The payment procedure expressly requires the payment voucher to be entered in the Vote Book.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressly required before payment is made?
options: MTEF approval for every individual transaction
questions.explanation: The source states that all payments must be pre-audited.

questions.question: The Treasury examines a payment voucher to determine whether the expenditure has been assigned the appropriate budget classification. What control is being performed?
options: Checking the correctness of budget classification
questions.explanation: The Treasury checks the payment voucher to ensure that the correct budget classifications have been applied to the expenditure.

questions.question: A payment is intended for a contractor who supplied goods to government. The officer processing the payment proposes making the cheque payable to himself instead. Which payment principle is violated?
options: Payment must be made to the right person or person entitled to be paid.
Payment must be entered in the MTEF.
Payment must be treated as capital revenue.
Payment must be made only through the PAC.
questions.explanation: The payment procedure requires payments to be made to the right persons or those entitled to be paid—such as suppliers, contractors and staff—not officials themselves or other insiders.

questions.question: After the payment transaction has been properly authorized and processed, the transaction must be posted into the—
questions.explanation: Posting the transaction into the Cash Book is one of the expressly listed payment procedures.

questions.question: Which event occurs immediately after the transaction is posted into the Cash Book, according to the sequence in the material?
options: A cheque is issued or a duly signed bank mandate transfers funds to the payee.
The PAC examines the public accounts.
The House of Assembly passes the Appropriation Law.
questions.explanation: The payment procedure lists issuance of a cheque or duly signed bank mandate to transfer funds to the payee after posting the transaction into the Cash Book.

questions.question: Following issuance of a cheque, which action is required of the payee?
options: Signing the cheque register and the appropriate section of the payment voucher
questions.explanation: The payee must sign the cheque register and the appropriate section of the payment voucher.

questions.question: What documentary evidence from the payee must ultimately be attached to the payment voucher?
questions.explanation: The payment procedure requires an official receipt from the payee to be attached to the payment voucher.

questions.question: A payment officer performs the following actions: Confirms availability of funds through the relevant warrant/AIE. Enters the payment voucher in the Vote Book. Ensures pre-audit. Treasury checks budget classification. Confirms the correct payee. Posts the transaction into the Cash Book. Issues a cheque/bank mandate. Obtains the payee's signature and official receipt. What is the best description of this sequence?
options: It substantially follows the prescribed government payment procedure.
It is the procedure for preparing the MTEF.
It is the procedure for retiring Special Imprest.
It is the procedure for preparing the Auditor-General's report.
questions.explanation: These steps correspond to the payment procedures listed in the material, from approval and funding evidence through voucher entry, pre-audit, Treasury checks, payment, signatures and receipt documentation.

questions.question: Accounting and reporting in government financial management refers primarily to the systematic process of—
options: recording, analyzing, summarizing and presenting financial transactions and information
questions.explanation: The source defines accounting and reporting as the systematic recording, analyzing, summarizing and presentation of financial transactions and information of public-sector entities.

questions.question: According to the material, accounting and reporting helps promote—
options: transparency, accountability and efficient use of public resources
questions.explanation: The source expressly states that accounting and reporting ensures transparency, accountability and efficient use of public resources.

questions.question: The primary purpose of government audit, as described in the material, is to provide assurance to—
questions.explanation: Government audit provides assurance to stakeholders such as citizens, lawmakers and oversight bodies concerning transparency, accountability and integrity of public funds and resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as something the audit process can help identify?
questions.explanation: The source states that audit helps identify financial irregularities, inefficiencies and areas for improvement in government financial management.

questions.question: The PAC is reviewing a State's public accounts and financial statements, paying particular attention to government revenue and expenditure. Which PAC function is being exercised?
questions.explanation: Examination of public accounts involves reviewing the State's public accounts and financial statements and scrutinizing government expenditures and revenues.

questions.question: The Auditor-General identifies an irregularity in the management of public funds and reports it to the PAC. What is the PAC specifically empowered to do in response?
options: Examine the Auditor-General's report and address identified irregularities or inefficiencies.
Convert the expenditure into capital receipts.
questions.explanation: The PAC examines reports from the Auditor-General and addresses irregularities or inefficiencies identified in the management of public funds.

questions.question: A government payment has gone through the following stages: approval by the designated authority; appropriate payment voucher; evidence of funds through warrant/AIE; Vote Book entry; pre-audit; Treasury verification of budget classification; payment to the person entitled; Cash Book posting; cheque/bank mandate; payee's signature; and attachment of the official receipt. Afterward, the State's financial records are subjected to accounting, reporting and audit, while the PAC examines the public accounts and Auditor-General's reports. Which statement BEST captures the control architecture represented by this scenario?
options: It combines transaction-level expenditure controls with subsequent accounting, audit and legislative oversight.
It represents only the procurement process.
It represents only the preparation of recurrent revenue.
It represents exclusively the MTEF process.
questions.explanation: The payment sequence establishes controls over an individual government expenditure, while accounting/reporting records and presents the transaction, audit provides assurance and identifies irregularities, and the PAC performs legislative financial oversight.

questions.question: According to the seminar material, financial management in government is fundamentally the process by which public resources are—
questions.explanation: The material defines financial management in government as the process by which public resources are planned, organized, directed and controlled to enhance efficient and effective public service delivery.

questions.question: A financial-management system is designed to help government raise, spend and manage financial resources while providing social services. Which combination of principles does the material associate with this process?
questions.explanation: The material states that government manages its financial resources for economic development and social services in an efficient, effective, accountable and transparent manner.

questions.question: A government financial officer is asked to identify the overall purpose behind controlling and managing public resources. Which answer best reflects the material?
options: To enhance efficient and effective public service delivery
To maximize personal financial benefits of public officers
To replace public services with private services
questions.explanation: Enhancing efficient and effective public service delivery is expressly identified as the purpose of the financial-management process.

questions.question: Which scenario best demonstrates the objective of building public trust through financial management?
options: Officials make financial decisions transparently and are held accountable for those decisions.
Officials conceal expenditure information from stakeholders.
Public funds are treated as personal funds.
questions.explanation: The material specifically identifies building public trust through transparent financial practices and holding officials accountable for their financial decisions.

questions.question: Government wants to prevent reckless spending, wastage and over-expenditure. Which combination of measures is expressly stated in the material?
options: Monitoring public expenditure, regular audits and stringent controls
Increasing loans, reducing audits and removing controls
Increasing imprest and eliminating expenditure monitoring
questions.explanation: These three measures are expressly identified as means of preventing reckless spending, wastage and over-expenditure.

questions.question: A government wants to maintain fiscal sustainability. Which course of action is most consistent with the material?
options: Borrow at the lowest cost, monitor debt levels and ensure debt servicing does not hinder public services.
Borrow as much as possible regardless of cost.
Ignore debt levels once funds are available.
Prioritize debt servicing even where public services are hindered.
questions.explanation: These are the specific measures identified under the objective of maintaining fiscal sustainability.

questions.question: Government has two proposed projects and chooses the one with a high expected return while aligning it with national goals. Which financial-management objective is being pursued?
options: Optimizing investment to promote socio-economic development
questions.explanation: The material says government should optimize investment for socio-economic development by prioritizing high-return projects and aligning investments with national goals.

questions.question: A financial officer insists that government funds must be managed according to applicable financial regulations and standards. Which objective does this represent?
questions.explanation: Compliance with legal frameworks through adherence to financial regulations and standards is expressly listed as an objective.

questions.question: A State introduces policies aimed at ensuring equitable distribution of public resources among its citizens. Which objective is most directly involved?
options: Promoting social equity, cohesion and stability
questions.explanation: The material identifies equitable distribution of public resources as a means of promoting social equity, cohesion and stability.

questions.question: A government establishes a sound internal-control system specifically to protect its property and other assets. Which objective does this support?
questions.explanation: The material expressly states that government should safeguard its assets by installing a sound system of internal control.

questions.question: Which statement correctly connects the Constitution with government financial management according to the seminar?
options: Sections 120–127 specify how money should be paid into the Consolidated Revenue Fund and how expenditure from it is authorized.
Sections 120–127 establish the Public Accounts Committee.
Sections 120–127 govern procurement of goods and services.
Sections 120–127 prescribe how personal advances are retired.
questions.explanation: This is precisely how the seminar describes Sections 120–127 of the 1999 Constitution.

questions.question: Which regulatory instrument provides detailed day-to-day rules on the collection, custody and disbursement of government funds in Akwa Ibom State?
options: Akwa Ibom State Financial Regulations, 2003 Edition
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically assigns this function to the Akwa Ibom State Financial Regulations, 2003 Edition.

questions.question: Which financial legislation is described as appropriating public monies for services to be rendered during the year to which the legislation applies?
questions.explanation: The seminar gives Annual and Supplementary Appropriation Acts as examples of financial legislation enacted to appropriate public monies for services during the applicable year.

questions.question: The Akwa Ibom State Audit Law 2021 requires the Accountant-General to submit the annual accounts to the—
options: Head of Budget Office for approval
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that the Audit Law demands the Accountant-General to submit the annual accounts to the State Auditor-General for audit.

questions.question: Which pairing is correctly matched?
options: Fiscal Responsibility Law 2000 — prudent management of State resources
Public Procurement Law 2007 — preparation of Final Accounts
Public Service Rules 2022 — issuance of warrants
Treasury circulars — conduct of State audits
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Akwa Ibom State Fiscal Responsibility Law 2000 provides for prudent management of the State's resources. It separately identifies the Procurement Law as ensuring probity in procurement, the Public Service Rules as governing public officers, and Treasury/Finance circulars as updating financial rules.

questions.question: The Governor has prepared and submitted the Executive Bill known as the Appropriation Bill. The State House of Assembly subsequently passes it. What happens next according to the material?
options: The Governor assents to it, after which it becomes the Appropriation Law for the financial year.
The Accountant-General converts it into an MTEF.
The Auditor-General audits it before it becomes law.
The PAC issues a warrant to the Governor.
questions.explanation: The material states that after the Appropriation Bill is passed, the Governor assents to it and it becomes the Appropriation Law for the financial year.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the financial-management chain stated in the seminar?
options: Governor → Commissioner for Finance → Accountant-General → Auditor-General → PAC
Governor → PAC → Accountant-General → Commissioner for Finance → Auditor-General
PAC → Governor → Auditor-General → Budget Office → Accountant-General
Auditor-General → Governor → PAC → Commissioner for Finance → Accountant-General
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Governor as the Chief Executive who submits the Appropriation Bill; the Commissioner for Finance receives delegated financial responsibilities and issues warrants; the Accountant-General prepares Government/Final Accounts; the Auditor-General audits them; and the Auditor-General's report is submitted to the PAC.

questions.question: A Permanent Secretary is responsible for ensuring that public funds under the ministry's control are protected and that expenditure is properly regulated. According to the seminar, the Permanent Secretary is acting as the ministry's—
questions.explanation: Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Departments are identified as the Accounting Officers of their Ministries and Departments, responsible for safeguarding public funds and regulating expenditure under their control.

questions.question: A financial discrepancy is identified in the management of public funds. The relevant officials are called before a committee to explain the discrepancy, and the committee conducts an investigation. Which body is exercising this function?
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that the PAC can summon public officials to explain discrepancies and conduct investigations into financial matters.

questions.question: A State financial-management system involves the following: Public resources are planned, organized, directed and controlled. Government identifies revenue sources and prioritizes essential services. Public expenditure is monitored and audited to prevent wastage and over-expenditure. The Governor submits an Appropriation Bill to the House of Assembly. The Commissioner for Finance issues warrants to the Accountant-General. The Accountant-General prepares the Government and Final Accounts. The State Auditor-General audits the public accounts and submits his report to the PAC. The PAC examines public accounts and can summon officials to explain discrepancies. Which statement BEST describes the entire framework?
options: It represents an integrated system of planning, resource management, expenditure control, accounting, audit and legislative oversight in government financial management.
It represents only the government's revenue-collection process.
It represents only the public procurement process.
It represents only the preparation and retirement of imprest.
questions.explanation: The seminar presents financial management in government as the planning, organization, direction and control of public resources for efficient and effective service delivery. It then sets out objectives involving revenue, expenditure, accountability and control, followed by the roles of the Governor, Commissioner for Finance, Accountant-General, Auditor-General and PAC within the government's financial-management framework.
